overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data reveals that space exploration, planetary 'what-if' hypotheticals, and extreme cosmic phenomena are significantly outperforming general psychology and standard science facts in both views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view). Specifically, hypothetical scenario framing ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme visual environments (diamond planets, burning ice, extreme darkness) generates the highest sustained traction. Older physiological and basic psychological facts show stagnant momentum.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved over 1,000 views rapidly with exceptionally high like ratios compared to older psychological facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme space hypothetical scenarios, focusing on sensory-rich, immersive world-building within the first 3 seconds.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (QXuqYERlqSo) captured high velocity and strong engagement within the recent 7-day window.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form pieces focusing on bizarre planetary weather, extreme densities, and light-absorbing anomalies.

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (ef3ND4qiRHc) yielded very low views and minimal engagement over the observation window.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard psychological tips and generic memory facts unless paired with a high-stakes visual or mystery element.
